post.summary: Built-in gateway tools plus the device tools the Agent may call.
``{url, username, password}`` of the running OpenCode instance, or null.
A new gateway token for Codex and OpenCode (which restarts to pick it up).
Whether Codex is connected to this gateway, and what is missing.

Add a device from its ``.tsdev`` package. The package is installed when needed, the
device gets generated ids and is connected at once.

Add a device from a ``.tsdev`` device package on this computer (absolute path). The
package's driver code runs inside testStand, so the operator confirms first.
The managed device's ``/device`` declaration as cached (read-only, §9.7).

What adding a device from a ``.tsdev`` would install: manifest, files, SHA-256 and any
problems. Writes nothing.
Registered devices (plugin instances) without connection status.
Installed device packages, with changes that wait for a restart.

Remove a device; the last device of a package also takes the package away (at the
next start, since its code may be loaded).
Create or update a device's settings; the operator confirms in testStand.
The monitor workspace: its panels (type, title, sources, settings) and layout.

Every device with the streams it declares (``known`` is false until the device was
connected once; the cached declaration is used while it is offline).

Change the workspace: ``operations`` apply in order (add / remove / update a panel,
add / remove its sources); ``remove`` then takes each stream off every panel and ``add``
puts it on the first panel that draws its type (a new one when none does); ``layout``
replaces the saved docking layout. A stream must belong to a registered device and,
once the device's streams are known, be one it declares and one the panel can draw.
Stays in the project buffer until the project is saved. Returns the workspace.
Recently opened project folders, newest first; open one with open_project.
Theme, layouts, recent projects and the model settings (never the key).

Save the OpenCode model settings; the key goes to the credential store. OpenCode
restarts, starts or stops to match, after this returns.

A run recording over ``[t0, t1]``, min/max downsampled to ``width`` pixel columns
(design doc 5.9.3); the live view is ``GET /api/live``.
Approve or decline a pending confirmation; only a human holds ``agents.manage``.
The Agent's high-risk operations waiting for the operator (design doc 8.4).
Validate an unsaved plan draft against current devices without saving it.
The operator's answer to a waiting ``ManualCheck`` (design §7.2); never an Agent's.
Validate ICD text (unsaved or ``name``'s file) and trial-decode sample records.
The active or latest test run, or null.
The current unit under test (serial number and attributes) runs are recorded for.
Each step execution of a run with its start/end time and outcome.
The data streams recorded during a run, with their keys for readRunStream.
The project's test flow (a project has one: ``flow``).
Records of one run stream, by key from listRunStreams, optionally windowed.

Judge a finished run's recordings again with the current assertions; the stored
verdict is not changed.
Write ``icd/<name>.icd.yaml``; an invalid ICD is rejected and nothing is written.

Replace a saved plan with a complete plan document at ``baseRevision``. Prefer
apply_test_plan_operations for edits; this is for the operator's editor.

The operator's answer to a wiring task: ``confirmed`` applies every change and saves
the project; ``rejected`` carries the operator's reason in ``message``.
The project's wiring change log: confirmed wiring tasks and manual edits.

Create one wiring task holding every change; the operator confirms or rejects it once.
Returns at once with the pending task.

Ask the operator to make wiring changes on the bench and wait for the answer. The call
returns only when the operator confirmed (the project wiring then holds the changes and is
saved) or rejected the request (``message`` says why); cancelling the call cancels the
task.
